message.content:
**CPU usage** is the percentage of time the processor spends doing useful work (running processes, executing code) versus being idle.  
Typical values:

| Usage | Interpretation |
|-------|----------------|
| 0 – 10 % | Idle / light background tasks |
| 10 – 30 % | Normal everyday use (web browsing, office apps) |
| 30 – 70 % | Heavy multitasking or moderate gaming |
| 70 – 90 % | High‑load workloads (video editing, large simulations) |
| 90 – 100 % | CPU saturated – performance may degrade |

---

### How to check CPU usage on Windows

| Method | What you’ll see | How to run |
|--------|-----------------|------------|
| **Task Manager** | Real‑time graph + % CPU per process | Press `Ctrl+Shift+Esc` → “Performance” tab → “CPU” |
| **PowerShell** | Counter value in real time | ```powershell\nGet-Counter '\Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time'\n``` |
| **WMIC** | One‑line numeric output | ```cmd\nwmic cpu get loadpercentage\n``` |

#### Example PowerShell command (via the tool)

If you want to run it from this chat interface, you can use the provided tool:

```json
{
  "name": "functions.cmd_controller_execute",
  "arguments": {
    "command": "powershell -Command \"Get-Counter '\\Processor(_Total)\\% Processor Time'\"",
    "unit": "N/A"
  }
}
```

(Replace the JSON with the actual call format required by your environment.)

---

### Quick tip

If you just need a quick snapshot without opening Task Manager, the `wmic` command is the simplest:

```cmd
wmic cpu get loadpercentage
```

It will print something like:

```
LoadPercentage
15
```

which means the CPU is currently at 15 % utilization.

Feel free to ask if you’d like help interpreting the numbers or troubleshooting high CPU usage!
